evals.name: relentless-me-mode-frontier-rounds
evals.prompt: /planning:interview me — I want to add rate limiting to the public API but haven't thought through the details.
evals.expected_output: In me-mode the skill runs a relentless frontier-rounds interview: each round asks every question whose prerequisites are settled as one numbered set in inline prose (not AskUserQuestion), each question leading with a recommendation and its basis, and grounds answers in the codebase where the code already answers a question.
expectations: Output asks the round's independent frontier questions together as one numbered set, not spread across separate turns
Each question leads with a recommended answer and a one-line basis
The round is asked inline in prose, not via a side-by-side AskUserQuestion card
Where a question is answerable from the codebase, the skill resolves it by inspection instead of spending a question on it

evals.name: auto-guard-never-folds-user-choice
evals.prompt: /planning:interview add a soft-delete flag to the accounts table. The intent is mostly clear — just lock the brief.
evals.expected_output: During synthesis, if a genuine user design decision with real tradeoffs and no codebase answer surfaces (e.g. cascade behavior for soft-deleted accounts), the skill STOPS and surfaces it as the user's to decide instead of silently folding it into the Brief as a captured assumption.
expectations: Output does NOT silently capture a real user design choice as an assumption in the Brief
When a genuine design decision with no codebase answer surfaces, the skill stops and surfaces it (asks it, or offers to run relentless me-mode)
Output distinguishes codebase-resolvable / conventional-default decisions (which it may synthesize) from genuine user decisions (which it must not)

evals.name: lock-mode-does-not-fudge-gap
evals.prompt: /planning:interview lock the brief for adding webhook retries — I've told you enough.
evals.expected_output: In lock mode the skill synthesizes the Brief directly without Q&A, but if a true unknown surfaces mid-synthesis it STOPS and surfaces the gap rather than guessing a value to fill it.
expectations: Output synthesizes the Brief directly rather than running a full Q&A loop
If a true unknown surfaces during synthesis, the skill stops and surfaces it rather than fabricating a value
Output does not fudge a gap to avoid interrupting the lock

evals.name: brief-persisted-not-plan
evals.prompt: /planning:interview lock a brief for adding a CSV export endpoint to the reports service.
evals.expected_output: The skill writes the Brief section (TLDR / Goal / Constraints / Acceptance criteria / Captured assumptions / Out-of-scope / Deferred questions) into PLAN.md and leaves the Plan section for /planning:plan — it produces the WHAT contract, not an implementation approach.
expectations: Output writes a Brief with goal, constraints, and testable acceptance criteria
Output does NOT draft an implementation plan / approach (that is /planning:plan's job)
Output recommends a next step (explore, research, or /planning:plan) rather than starting to code

evals.name: dependent-questions-split-across-rounds
evals.prompt: /planning:interview me about the caching approach for the product catalog — the cache key depends on the eviction policy which depends on the read pattern.
evals.expected_output: Because these decisions form a dependency chain (each question's framing depends on the previous answer), the skill splits them across rounds — the prerequisite question first, each dependent question only after its prerequisite is answered — and never batches a question into the same round as a question it depends on, nor renders them as an AskUserQuestion card without the user opt-in.
expectations: Output asks the prerequisite decision first and defers each dependent decision to a later round, after its prerequisite is answered
Output does NOT batch a question into the same round as a question it depends on
Output does NOT use an AskUserQuestion card absent the use_ask_user_question opt-in
Each question still leads with a recommendation and basis

evals.name: skips-truly-mechanical-work
evals.prompt: /planning:interview I need to fix a single spelling typo in a code comment in utils.ts — no behavior change, just correcting one misspelled word.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes this as truly mechanical (a comment typo, no behavior change) and declines to gate it with an interview, telling the user it needs no brief.
expectations: Output identifies the task as mechanical / non-behavioral (a comment typo)
Output does NOT run a Q&A loop or produce a Brief for it
Output tells the user the task does not warrant an interview

evals.name: engineering-term-resolution-delegates
evals.prompt: /planning:interview me — in this engineering task we resolved that Subscriber is canonical and Member is rejected. Continue the interview after preserving that decision.
evals.expected_output: Invokes /domain-driven-design:curate-language immediately for the resolved engineering vocabulary, then resumes the interview at the current round. It does not write a parallel glossary format itself, and a general-domain session would not mutate repo docs.
expectations: Invokes /domain-driven-design:curate-language immediately for the resolved term
Does not prescribe or reimplement glossary format/location in the interview skill
Resumes the interview loop after the vocabulary update
Keeps the repository write explicitly scoped to an engineering session

evals.name: facts-looked-up-decisions-asked
evals.prompt: /planning:interview me — migrate our config loader to support environment overrides. I don't remember what format the current config file uses, and I'm torn on whether overrides should win over file values or vice versa.
evals.expected_output: The skill resolves the current config format from the codebase itself (a fact — read, stated, never asked) and puts the override-precedence choice to the user as a round question with a recommendation (a decision — real tradeoffs, never resolved on the user's behalf).
expectations: The current config format is resolved by inspecting the codebase and stated as a finding, not asked as a question
The override-precedence choice is asked as a question with a recommendation, not silently decided
Output does not ask the user to confirm a fact the code already answers

evals.name: recommends-session-config-engineering-downstream
evals.prompt: /planning:interview me — I need to re-architect our authorization layer to support per-resource policies across three services, and I'm unsure which invariants can change safely.
evals.expected_output: This is an engineering session (a code re-architecture that hands off downstream per Step 5), so at the stop/handoff boundary the skill recommends how to configure the downstream execution session — a model tier and effort level chosen per the capability-vs-thoroughness distinction, plus the advisor pairing when the main model is a faster tier, deriving the current model names and accepted pairings from the live official docs rather than pinned values, framed as an advisory delta the user applies, and degrading gracefully (durable distinction + a visible note) if the docs cannot be fetched rather than halting or guessing a model name.
expectations: Because this is an engineering session that hands off downstream, output frames the recommendation as configuring the downstream execution session (not the current/next session)
Output recommends a model tier and effort level, distinguishing capability (model) from thoroughness (effort)
Output recommends advisor pairing when the main model is a faster tier, rather than a faster main with no advisor
Current model names / tiers / pairings are sourced from the live official docs, not pinned in the skill
On a doc-fetch failure the skill degrades to the durable distinction with a visible note and does not halt the interview or guess a model name
The recommendation is framed as advisory (applied via /model, /advisor, effort setting), not as a read of the user's current config

evals.name: recommends-session-config-general-current-session
evals.prompt: /planning:interview me — help me decide our company's org structure: whether to reorganize from functional teams into cross-functional product squads, and how to sequence that transition across roughly 200 people. This is an organizational-strategy decision, not a code change.
evals.expected_output: This is a general/terminal session (an org-strategy decision with no build surface, explicitly not a code change, so per Step 5 nothing downstream exists to configure). At the stop boundary the skill still recommends session config, but frames it as the current/next session applied now — a model tier and effort level per the capability-vs-thoroughness distinction, plus the advisor pairing when the main model is a faster tier, deriving current model names and accepted pairings from the live official docs rather than pinned values, framed as an advisory delta the user applies (via /model, the effort setting, /advisor), and degrading gracefully (durable distinction + a visible note) if the docs cannot be fetched. It does NOT frame the recommendation as configuring a downstream execution session that will never exist.
expectations: Recognizes this as a general/terminal session (no downstream execution session exists per Step 5) and frames the recommendation as config for the current/next session, applied now — NOT a downstream execution session
Output recommends a model tier and effort level, distinguishing capability (model) from thoroughness (effort)
Output recommends advisor pairing when the main model is a faster tier, rather than a faster main with no advisor
Current model names / tiers / pairings are sourced from the live official docs, not pinned in the skill
On a doc-fetch failure the skill degrades to the durable distinction with a visible note and does not halt the interview or guess a model name
The recommendation is framed as advisory (applied via /model, /advisor, effort setting), not as a read of the user's current config
